close_reason: Fixed in 5e18f72: chose option (a) — typed ContactCard.keywords as Option<HashMap<String, bool>> matching the sibling members and address_book_ids fields and the RFC 9553 §2.8.2 String[Boolean] closed shape. PLAN.md was already aspirationally correct; code now matches. Updated the test (renamed keywords_roundtrips_as_string_bool_map) to operate on the typed field directly.
description: crate-jmap-contacts-types/PLAN.md line 244 documents 'pub keywords: Option<HashMap<String, bool>>' on ContactCard. crate-jmap-contacts-types/src/card.rs:170 actually declares 'pub keywords: Option<serde_json::Value>'. RFC 9553 §2.8.2 defines keywords as String[Boolean] — a closed shape that could safely be typed. The sibling fields 'members' (card.rs:65) and 'address_book_ids' (card.rs:43) are typed as HashMap<_, bool>, so 'keywords' is the odd one out within the same struct for the same wire shape. Two options: (a) tighten code to match PLAN — promote keywords to HashMap<String, bool> for consistency with members; the localizations promotion at 06c9385 set the precedent. (b) loosen PLAN to match code — explain why keywords stays Value (round-trip fidelity vs spec extension). Either is fine, but the drift between PLAN and code is a maintainer trap: future-you will read PLAN, ship a sub-tle bug, and not know which is authoritative.
title: PLAN.md ContactCard listing claims keywords: Option<HashMap<String,bool>>, code has Option<serde_json::Value>
